chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Poetry is not recited at night, nor is it recited in the month of Ramadan neither by night nor by day.' Isma'il said to him: 'O my father, for it is among us.' He said: 'Even if it is among us.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting poetry during the month of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a general prohibition against reciting poetry at night and entirely during Ramadan, emphasizing spiritual focus over leisure. When Isma'il ibn Yahya argued that poetry was a common cultural practice among the Shia, the Imam affirmed the ruling regardless of its prevalence, highlighting that customary usage does not exempt one from religious etiquette. This hadith underscores the importance of maintaining reverence and avoiding distractions during the holy month, even in matters of cultural expression.
